rationale: Ground truth carries no substantive concerns (just an approval), so both candidates score recall=1.0 trivially and both go well beyond it by independently surfacing the same real defect: state.serving_tokenization=None in pure-diffusion mode still lets _create_speech_error_json_response call base(raw_request).create_error_response() unguarded, reproducing the 500 this PR claims to fix. Both also flag that the regression tests still mock api_server_module.base, so the fix isn't actually regression-tested. Y is slightly more precise/actionable: it anchors every major/minor finding to specific file:line evidence with an explicit validated/refuted claim ledger, adds a distinct, well-grounded major finding (create_chat_completion's handler-None branch returns a bare ErrorResponse instead of a 404 JSON, a real behavioral gap in code this diff touches) and ships GitHub-suggestion-formatted diffs. X's unique additions (version-pin/CI speculation, a sibling openai_serving_* rename audit) are honestly hedged as unverified leads, which keeps them non-fabricated but lowers their evidentiary weight and actionability compared to Y's more concretely verified extras.
